title: A robust protocol for the generation of human midbrain organoids
protocol: Detach NESCs using Accutase when cultures reach 80-90% confluence.
Count viable cells via standard Trypan Blue protocol using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Dilute 9 ×10^5 cells in 15 ml of N2B27 maintenance medium (for 100 wells).
Transfer 150 μl of cell suspension into each well of the 96-well ULA plate.
Change media every 2nd day by removing 2/3 volume and replacing with fresh N2B27 maintenance media without touching the colony.
Cut Parafilm squares approximately 5×5 cm big, enough for one 96-well plate.
Spray the Parafilm squares with 70% ethanol and place them under the biosafety cabinet.
Allow the ethanol on the Parafilm to evaporate completely.
Place one square of Parafilm over an empty tip tray using sterile forceps.
Create small dimples (4×4 dimples per Parafilm square) by pressing a gloved finger over the holes.
Place the Geltrex stock vial on ice at 4°C in the fridge and let it thaw overnight (8–14 h).
Transfer 3D colonies to an untreated 24-well tissue culture plate (TCP) at day 6 of organoid culture.
Distribute 500 μL of pre-warmed (37°C) N2B27 maintenance medium to each well of the TCP.
Cut a 1 ml pipet tip using sterile scissors.
Transfer each single 3D colony from the 96-well plate to a single well of the 24-well TCP using the cut pipet tip.
Place one dimpled Parafilm square in a fresh Petri dish.
Place a single 3D colony from the TCP into each dimple using a cut 1 ml pipet tip.
Add Geltrex to each colony after aspiration of the residual culturing medium.
Place the polymerized Geltrex/colony droplets in medium.
Shake the Petri dish to detach the embedded colonies from the Parafilm.
Transfer embedded colonies in individual wells using a 1 mL pipet with a cut tip.
Remove the medium around the 3D colony using a 10 μL pipet tip.
Add 35 μl of Geltrex around the 3D colony and keep the colony centered.
Incubate at 37°C for 25 min to allow Geltrex to polymerize.
Collect Geltrex droplets with embedded colonies by flipping Parafilm into a new Petri dish filled with pre-warmed DMEM/F12.
Incubate at 37°C for 25 min after transferring the colonies.
Remove Geltrex droplets from Parafilm by shaking slightly until they fall off.
Transfer a single embedded colony per well in a 24-well TCP using a cut 1 ml pipet tip.
Replace DMEM/F12 with 500 μL per well of N2B27 maintenance medium.
Keep organoids in an incubator under static conditions until differentiation begins (day 10).
On the second day after embedding (Day 10 of organoid culture), replace N2B27 maintenance media with N2B27 differentiation media + PMA.
Try to remove as much media as possible before adding fresh media during media change.
Gently aspirate and add a fresh medium using a 1 ml pipet due to the fragility of the matrix and small size of organoids.
At day 12 of organoid culture, perform a full media change with fresh N2B27 differentiation media + PMA (500 μL per well).
On day 14 of organoid culture, fully change media to fresh N2B27 differentiation media + PMA (500 μL per well) and place the organoids on a horizontal shaker set at 80 rpm inside the incubator.
Shake the cultures to ensure optimal nutrient supply and organoid growth.
Sterilize the shaker before placing it in the incubator.
Perform a full media change using fresh N2B27 differentiation media without PMA at day 16 of organoid culture.
Leave out PMA for subsequent media changes after day 16.
Change the media every 3-4 days using 500 μL of N2B27 differentiation media without PMA for long-term culture.
Increase the volume of fresh media to 600 μl per well after day 30.
Monitor media color changes to determine nutrient consumption and metabolic activity.
Increase media volume to 600 μl per well if media turns yellow before regular media change.
